main_text.p: tantùmnon desperatis temporibus sapientissimè, prudentissimèque fungentem; omnes mirantur. Te denique fortissima Heluetiorum gens tanquam unicum, & coelo delapsum fidei,constantiæ, veritatis, grauitatis, &c, ut uno verbo dicam, veteris illius Fracicæ generositatis,quę pridem defecisse in nostra gente artibus corrupta exoticis,videbatur,exemplar intuetur, sufpicitque. Quid ego nunc commemorem, non iuris ciuilis tantùm, sed plurimarum artium honestissimarum accuratam cognitionem? quid summum illum amorem, ardorémque in litteras, & cùm plurima teneas,plura in dies discendi defide

page.notes: The first word is a fragment continuing from the previous page. Several words are uncertain and were not marked with [?] because the scan is clear enough: "Fracicæ" (possibly "Francicæ"), "sufpicitque" (possibly "suspicitque"), "ardorémque" (accent as printed). The last line reads "fide" after the hyphen "de-", so the printed word is "defide" split across lines; it is kept as one word, with the line-end hyphen removed. The text is one paragraph with no printed indent visible.
